title: Toronto’s 2 mayoral front-runners to face off in debate hosted by CBC Toronto
summary: The two top candidates in Toronto’s mayoral race are set to face off in a debate inside the CBC Broadcasting Centre on Thursday.

blocks.text: Toronto
The two top candidates in Toronto’s mayoral race are set to face off in a debate inside the CBC Broadcasting Centre on Thursday.
Debate will be livestreamed on Thursday from 12 p.m. to 1 p.m. ET
Toronto votes: Mayoral candidates face off
Incumbent mayor Olivia Chow and Coun. Brad Bradford will go head-to-head at noon to discuss key issues affecting the city.
The debate is happening at a crucial moment in the election. Advance voting is underway across the city until Sunday, and Chris Alexander officially dropped out of the mayor’s race on Tuesday.
The former MP had been polling at third place and his votes are now up for grabs.

The discussion will be moderated by Chris Glover, host of CBC Radio’s Metro Morning. The program will dig into both candidates' platforms and provide an opportunity for the audience to glean a sense of their personalities.

items: Is Toronto broken or thriving? Candidates can’t agree

blocks.text: The debate will run until 1 p.m. and will be streamed live on the CBC News app, CBC Gem, YouTube and TikTok, as well as on TV and Radio. Click here to learn more about where you can watch the program.
Tune in Thursday afternoon to see how the candidates respond to pressing questions about issues that affect the lives of Torontonians.
It will also be available on demand afterwards for those who can't watch live.
A head-to-head rivalry
At past debates, the discussion between Chow and Bradford has, at times, become heated as the opponents make their case for why they should be Toronto's choice for mayor.
Chow and Bradford have often clashed over their approaches to public transit and safety, and have made jabs about each other’s track records while at city hall.
They’ve also butted heads over taxes and city finances.

Throughout the course of the campaign, Bradford has been critical of Chow’s increases to property taxes over the years — which were raised 2.2 per cent in 2026, down from 6.9 per cent in 2025 and 9.5 per cent in 2024. The latter was the highest increase in 25 years.
Previous debates between Olivia Chow and Brad Bradford have become heated. (Evan Mitsui, Alex Lupul/CBC)
This time around, Chow is promising to keep property tax increases "at or around" the rate of inflation. In response, Bradford's team said voters "have every reason not to take her word for it."

In past debates, Chow has pointed at Bradford’s past role as vice chair on the budget committee under former mayor John Tory and said her opponent holds responsibility for sending the city into the red and creating the circumstances that drove the tax increase.
When Chow first took office, the city was dealing with a budget deficit of $1.8 billion post-pandemic and the city’s credit rating has improved since Chow's election win.

blocks.text: Chow has been critical of Bradford’s promise to cut Torontonians' water bills by 25 per cent — a plan Bradford says he'll pay for by changing how the city deals with debt and increasing borrowing for capital projects.
Chow's team has said Bradford won't be able to deliver on that promise and has said the councillor will "say anything to get elected."
